qubit-control-neutral-r3.scope: Final public specification and both controls reviewed; path phase signs independently derived; all20 hidden Fock references rerun at56 and72 levels.
findings: Conditional oscillator evolution is exp(i*c²*s²*(omega*t−sin(omega*t)))*D(c*s*(exp(−i*omega*t)−1))*R(t). Composition yields alpha2+alpha1*exp(−i*omega*t2) and the positive BCH phase Im(alpha2*conj(transported alpha1)).
Cyclic thermal tracing gives the further positive Im(alpha_path_p*conj(alpha_path_q)) term. The oracle implements both cross pieces with consistent path ordering and rotation/readout conventions.

The shortcut retains the complete positive classical covariance kernel and each interval self-phase, but omits both inter-interval retarded phase pieces. It is an average over correlated classical drives with local diagonal unitary phases, hence completely positive and trace preserving, rather than an invalid density-matrix edit.

Single-interval calibration includes both individual and paired probes, validating the local quantum phase while leaving cross-interval response unobserved. Individual-probe dephasing records also identify the positive coupling scale monotonically.

The public Hamiltonian, uncoupled thermal preparation, continuously evolving bath, held weights, instantaneous pulses, no counterterms and detector projection fully determine the experiment. No reset or missing bath assumption is needed.

Private Fock cutoff56 versus72 differs by at most4.95e-14 over all20 hidden cases; agreement with the oracle is at most3.52e-14. Independent80→104 corner convergence and density positivity checks are recorded in the author report.

The shortcut robustly fails the echo group; the other two groups pass at the nominal fit. At least one failing group suffices for the unchanged all-groups grader. The256 worst-group minimum .03604 exceeds the .03 threshold; no claim is made that every hidden group fails.
